summary: Robin D. S. Yates is a sinologist and historian-archaeologist who completed his PhD at Harvard University around 1975–1980. Around 2002, he held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University.

Robin Dunbar studied at Magdalen College School, Magdalen College, and completed his doctoral studies under John Hurrell Crook around 1969–1974. He later held an academic post at University College London from around 1987 to 1994.
Roderick Henry Macleod was an Indologist who completed an M.A. at the University of Cambridge around 1913–1915, having served there as a Lecturer in Indian Law in 1913.

Philosopher Roderick M. Chisholm studied at Brown University and Harvard University (PhD ~1938–1942). He taught at Brown University (~1947–1986), the Barnes Foundation (~1946), the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~1986–1990), and was an Honorarprofessor at the University of Graz (1974).

Roderick S. Bucknell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held an academic post at the University of Queensland from around 1976 to 2002, serving as Associate Professor from around 1995 to 2002.

Roderick Whitfield is a scholar of sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was affiliated with the British Museum (attested 1986), the University of London (attested 2010), and SOAS University of London, where he is Professor Emeritus.

Indologist Roger Billard studied at INALCO, the EPHE, and under Louis Renou. He held posts in the manuscript department of the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1945–1951) and at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1952–1979).
Roger Bischoff is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied traditionally under Mother Sayamagyi and U Chit Tin. In 1995, he was attested as an Assistant Teacher at the International Meditation Centre.

Roger Brown was a linguist who completed his undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Michigan between 1945 and 1952. He subsequently held a long-term academic appointment at Harvard University from 1962 to 1994.

Linguist and Indologist Roger Goossens completed his PhD at the Université libre de Bruxelles (~1921–1926), studying under Émile Boisacq, Paul-Émile Dumont, and Henri Grégoire. In 1945, he became Professor of Greek at the Université libre de Bruxelles.

Roger Heim studied at the École Centrale Paris and the Science Faculty of Paris. He was affiliated with the Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle from around 1929 to 1970, serving as its director between around 1950 and 1965.
Roger Jeffery is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Edinburgh in 1985. He has held a post at the University of Edinburgh since 1972, where he is now Professor Emeritus.

Roger R. Jackson studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1983) under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, he held posts at Fairfield University (attested 1986) and Carleton College (attested 1990–2017).

Roger T. Ames is a philosopher and sinologist who studied at UBC, NTU, CUHK, and SOAS under D. C. Lau (PhD 1978). He was a long-time professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1978–2016) and later taught at Peking University.

Rohana Seneviratne is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Peradeniya, Saga, Liverpool, and Oxford (DPhil 2015). He was a tutor at Liverpool and invigilator at Oxford, serving as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Peradeniya (2022–2024).
Rohit Saluja is a scholar in the fields of computational studies and Indology. He holds academic and research affiliations with the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.

Roland Barthes was a philosopher and linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at the CNRS (~1952–1959), the EHESS (~1962–1976), and the Collège de France (1976–1980).

Roland Ferenczi studied ancient history and Indology at the University of Pécs and Eötvös Loránd University. In 2024, he was an MSCA Postdoctoral Researcher at the University of Hamburg and a department head and curator at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.

Roland Grubb Kent studied at Swarthmore College and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (1903). Specializing in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he taught at Penn (1902–1947) and Bryn Mawr College (1910–1914).

Linguist Roland Harweg studied under Alfred Schmitt (~1954–1958) and Peter Hartmann (~1958–1963). He held academic posts at the University of Münster from around 1963 to 1969 and at Ruhr University Bochum from around 1969 to 1999.
